featured.title: Hormuz Talks Offer Hope for Global Energy Markets
featured.description: Iran and Oman are discussing arrangements that could allow more shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway remains heavily disrupted, but diplomatic efforts have raised hopes that traffic could gradually improve.

breaking_news.title: Hormuz Talks Offer Hope for Energy Markets
breaking_news.description: Iran and Oman are continuing discussions over arrangements that could allow more shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. No final reopening agreement has been reached, and vessel traffic remains far below normal levels.

breaking_news.title: Oil Prices Continue to Fall
breaking_news.description: Oil prices have declined for a fourth consecutive day as markets react to the possibility of improved shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude has traded around the high-$80s per barrel.

breaking_news.title: Russian NORSI Refinery Hit by Drone Attack
breaking_news.description: Russia's NORSI refinery has suspended crude processing following a Ukrainian drone attack, according to industry sources cited by Reuters. The disruption could add pressure to regional fuel supplies.

world.title: Hormuz Talks Offer Hope for Global Energy Markets
world.description: Iran and Oman are working on arrangements that could create a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz. The discussions are being closely watched because the waterway is a critical route for global energy supplies.

world.title: Oil Markets React to Hormuz Developments
world.description: Crude prices have fallen as investors assess diplomatic efforts surrounding the Strait of Hormuz. The decline reflects hopes of improved energy flows, although the situation remains uncertain.

world.title: Ukraine War Continues to Affect Regional Energy Supplies
world.description: The war between Russia and Ukraine continues to affect energy infrastructure and fuel markets. A Ukrainian drone attack has disrupted crude processing at Russia's NORSI refinery.

usa.title: US Watches Hormuz Developments Closely
usa.description: Washington continues to monitor developments surrounding Iran and the Strait of Hormuz as diplomatic efforts seek to reduce disruption to international shipping and energy supplies.

usa.title: AI Investment Remains a Major US Market Story
usa.description: Investors continue to examine whether enormous spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure will generate sustainable long-term growth for major technology companies.

europe.title: European Energy Markets Watch Strait of Hormuz
europe.description: European governments and energy companies continue monitoring developments around the Strait of Hormuz because prolonged disruption could affect fuel prices, gas supplies and inflation.

europe.title: Qatar Gas Disruption Raises European Energy Concerns
europe.description: Disruption affecting Qatar's LNG industry is creating additional uncertainty for European energy markets and global gas supplies.

africa.title: Nigeria's Kidnapping Crisis Remains a Major Security Concern
africa.description: Nigerian security forces are continuing rescue operations following reported mass kidnappings in Niger State. Authorities are still working to establish the full number of people abducted.

africa.title: Nigeria Kidnapping Ransom Payments Raise Concern
africa.description: A study reported by Reuters found that Nigerian kidnappers collected almost $5.8 million in ransom payments from civilian abductions over the past year, highlighting the financial dimension of the country's security crisis.

africa.title: Dangote Refinery Strengthens Nigeria's Fuel Export Position
africa.description: Nigeria's petroleum-product exports by sea have increased sharply since 2023, with the Dangote refinery contributing significantly to the growth.

africa.title: MTN Considers Banking Expansion in Africa
africa.description: MTN Group is considering banking licences in selected African markets as the telecommunications company expands its financial-services operations.

business.title: Global Markets Watch Oil and Hormuz Talks
business.description: Investors are watching oil prices and diplomatic developments around the Strait of Hormuz. The possibility of improved shipping has eased some concerns about prolonged energy disruption.

business.title: Energy Supply Risks Remain
business.description: Despite falling crude prices, global energy markets remain vulnerable to further disruption because shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains well below normal levels.

business.title: Kidnapping Has a Growing Economic Dimension in Nigeria
business.description: New research into ransom payments highlights the financial incentives behind kidnapping and the economic challenge facing Nigerian security agencies and affected communities.

technology.title: Artificial Intelligence Remains a Major Investment Story
technology.description: Companies and investors continue to pour enormous amounts of money into AI chips, computing infrastructure and data centres while markets look for evidence of sustainable returns.

technology.title: Technology Earnings Under Global Investor Focus
technology.description: Major technology companies remain under close scrutiny as investors assess AI demand, infrastructure spending and the long-term profitability of the sector.

morning_summary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morning_summary.description: Energy, security and economic uncertainty dominate today's global picture. The biggest immediate development is the continuing discussion between Iran and Oman over possible arrangements for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices have moved lower on hopes of improved traffic, although the waterway remains heavily disrupted. Nigeria continues to deal with a serious kidnapping crisis, while new research highlights the financial scale of ransom payments. The disruption at Russia's NORSI refinery adds another pressure point to regional fuel supplies, while artificial intelligence remains one of the world's biggest technology investment stories.

big_question: Can diplomacy succeed in easing the energy crisis, or will geopolitical tensions continue to keep global fuel prices under pressure?
